From 4cbb5050bffc49c716381ea2ecb07306dd46f83a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Amadeusz=20S=C5=82awi=C5=84ski?=
 <amadeuszx.slawinski@linux.intel.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2024 16:26:21 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: Intel: avs: Set name of control as in topology
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

When creating controls attached to widgets, there are a lot of rules if
they get their name prefixed with widget name or not. Due to that
controls ended up with weirdly looking names like "ssp0_fe DSP Volume",
while topology set it to "DSP Volume".

Fix this by setting no_wname_in_kcontrol_name to true in avs topology
widgets which disables unwanted behaviour.

Fixes: be2b81b519d7 ("ASoC: Intel: avs: Parse control tuples")
Signed-off-by: Amadeusz Sławiński <amadeuszx.slawinski@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240418142621.2487478-1-amadeuszx.slawinski@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/intel/avs/topology.c b/sound/soc/intel/avs/topology.c
index 13061bd1488b..42b42903ae9d 100644
--- a/sound/soc/intel/avs/topology.c
+++ b/sound/soc/intel/avs/topology.c
@@ -1582,6 +1582,8 @@ static int avs_widget_load(struct snd_soc_component *comp, int index,
 	if (!le32_to_cpu(dw->priv.size))
 		return 0;
 
+	w->no_wname_in_kcontrol_name = true;
+
 	if (w->ignore_suspend && !AVS_S0IX_SUPPORTED) {
 		dev_info_once(comp->dev, "Device does not support S0IX, check BIOS settings\n");
 		w->ignore_suspend = false;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `sound/soc/intel/avs/topology.c`**
   - A new line was added to the `avs_widget_load` function, specifically setting the `no_wname_in_kcontrol_name` property of the widget (`w`) to `true`. This change ensures that the control names created for the widgets do not get prefixed with the widget name, addressing the issue of controls having undesirably formatted names.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `topology.c` directly addresses the bug described in the patch, which was caused by the naming convention of controls attached to widgets. By setting `no_wname_in_kcontrol_name` to `true`, the patch aligns the control names with the intended names defined in the topology, thus fixing the issue of controls having names like "ssp0_fe DSP Volume" instead of the desired "DSP Volume". This change is a corrective measure following the previous commit identified in the patch as causing the problem.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
w->no_wname_in_kcontrol_name = false;
```
Reason:
The default setting of the `no_wname_in_kcontrol_name` property is false, which causes the widget name to be prefixed to the control names. This results in undesirably formatted names like "ssp0_fe DSP Volume" instead of the intended "DSP Volume".

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
w->no_wname_in_kcontrol_name = true;
```
Reason:
By setting `no_wname_in_kcontrol_name` to true, the unwanted behavior of prefixing the widget name to the control names is disabled, allowing the control names to be set as intended in the topology, thus resolving the issue.
